title: Historical paths humankind passed over time
competency: Examine the stages of the genus Homo and the sites in Ethiopia where their fossils were found.

keywords.def: The "handy human being", the oldest human being, able to make tools.
The "upright walking human being". First to use fire and to leave Africa.
The "wise human being", very similar to modern humans.

ideas.name: Three stages of the genus Homo

en.text: The genus Homo has three species: Homo habilis, Homo erectus and Homo sapiens. Homo habilis, the handy human, made tools. Homo erectus walked upright, used fire and left Africa. Homo sapiens, the wise human, is like modern people.

screens.title: Who used fire first?
screens.ask: Which early human was the first to master fire?
screens.after: Homo erectus first mastered fire. It was also the first to leave Africa.

screens.title: 2.1.3 Historical paths humankind passes over time
paras: The genus Homo has different species: Homo habilis, Homo erectus and Homo sapiens.

screens.title: The three species
table: Oldest human being, in Africa. Fossils: Olduvai Gorge (Tanzania), Lake Turkana (Kenya), Omo valley (Ethiopia).
First to master fire; first to migrate out of Africa. Fossils in Ethiopia: Omo Basin, Melka-Kunture, Konso-Gardula, Middle Awash.
Very similar to modern humans. Fossils: Awash and Omo valleys, near Dire Dawa.

screens.title: Modern human beings
paras: Modern human beings are different from their ancestors in many ways.
They have large brains. They are bi-pedal and walk erect.
They use languages, develop culture and invent tools.
They pass knowledge from generation to generation.
screens.note: Focus: Homo habilis made tools; Homo erectus walked upright; knowledge is the mark of Homo sapiens.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The "handy human being", the oldest human being, able to make tools.
The "upright walking human being". First to use fire and to leave Africa.
The "wise human being", very similar to modern humans.

screens.why: Each species has one key feature in the Focus box.
screens.clue: Habilis = handy, erectus = upright, sapiens = wise.

screens.title: Put the stages in order (oldest first)
screens.why: Homo habilis is the oldest, then Homo erectus, then Homo sapiens.
screens.clue: Start with the oldest, the "handy" human.

screens.text: Where in Ethiopia were Homo erectus fossils found? Tap all.
screens.why: The book lists Omo Basin, Melka-Kunture, Konso-Gardula and Middle Awash.
screens.clue: Four sites; none of them is in the far north-west.

screens.text: Which one is NOT a feature of modern human beings?
screens.why: The book lists large brains, walking on two legs, language, culture, tools and passing on knowledge. Large jaws are not listed.
screens.clue: Read the list of features of modern humans.

screens.text: A fossil shows a creature that walked upright and used fire, but could not use language. Which species fits best?
screens.why: Upright walking and fire belong to Homo erectus. Language belongs to Homo sapiens. Homo habilis is known for tools, not fire.
screens.clue: Which species is known for fire and walking upright?

test.text: Which species was the first to migrate from Africa to other parts of the world?

notes.text: The book prints "Olduvia Gorge in Tanzana", "lake Turkan", "Home erectus" and "wake erect"; shown as Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania, Lake Turkana, Homo erectus and walk erect.

The book says modern humans appeared about 40,000 years ago; the oldest Homo sapiens fossils (Omo Kibish, Ethiopia) are about 195,000 years old or more. The date is left out of the lesson; teacher to discuss.
Activity 2.1 B Q2 (mark sites on a map of Africa) cannot be done in the app; left out.
Figure 2.2 (march of progress) becomes an ordering question.
